top_needs.title: Practice efficiency gains and ROI with DM-monitored braces or aligners versus standard recall
top_needs.brands_and_products: Damon, ormco, Spark, Angel, Invisalign, clearcorrect, suresmile, KLOwen, Lightforce, SmartSTL, Aliwell, Virtualcare, NHS
top_needs.metrics_sought: chair time reduction, appointment frequency, ROI, profitability, time saving, visit reduction, ongoing monitoring costs vs benefits, staff efficiency, diary changes, rentability, adaptive aligner change, average visit reduction
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors are skeptical that DM will actually save them time or money, reduce appointments, or improve practice profitability. They want to see hard data that these workflow and financial benefits are real and not just marketing claims.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, case study, white paper, No format preference specified — reps asked for any available evidence
sample_queries: How much chair time reduction achieved
How can I make DM work in a practice with 8 chairs and 15 assistants in a way that they really get the real benefits and make it work financially as well in The Netherlands?
Could you provide any data demonstrating improved patient compliance with DM or its impact on patient outcomes
Are Damon brackets more efficient than other brands?
Reduced chair time, recent studies, practice efficiencies for aligners
top_needs.gap_assessment: There is a need for robust, comparative studies quantifying time and cost savings, especially for specific brands and in diverse practice settings. More localized or specialty-specific ROI data would help address persistent skepticism.

top_needs.title: Accuracy and reliability of DM’s AI for clinical monitoring and diagnosis versus human assessment
top_needs.metrics_sought: AI accuracy, specificity and sensitivity, reliability, occlusal assessment, class I goal, FDA application, accuracy of scanning, aligner unseat tracking
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors question whether DM’s AI is as accurate as a clinician in detecting clinical changes, tracking aligner fit, or identifying issues. Some are concerned about regulatory validation and want proof the AI is reliable for diagnosis and triage.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, peer-reviewed, white paper, No format preference specified — reps asked for any available evidence
sample_queries: Information on the accuracy of DM, a patient has questioned the ability of the AI to detect clinical observations
Specificity and sensitivity results for FDA application

Occlusal Assessment: A quantitative study validating the AI’s accuracy in detecting malocclusions (midline deviation, overbite, overjet, and canine relationship) found that the mean bias across all parameters was less than 0.5 mm, confirming its reliability as a remote diagnosis and triage tool.
How accurate is DentalMonitorings AI and will it save me money
How accurate is SmartSTL AI
top_needs.gap_assessment: More head-to-head studies comparing AI versus orthodontist assessments, especially for specific clinical tasks and regulatory endpoints, are needed. Evidence for pediatric and special case accuracy is also limited.
